messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — ap-northeast-3 azc (proxy path) 5xx spike detected. Error rate: 34% over 5m. Affected service: inference-proxy (fronting public API). Paging on-call: @oncall-sre. Incident ID: INC-20260315-001

oncall-sre: acked. I’m on it, moving to incident channel #incident-1712009876.

mike: joining. seeing 503s from our healthcheck in ap-northeast-3 azc, curl samples show upstream reset.

anjali: same — customer reports for dedicated pools in ap-northeast-3. Latency also up to 8s.

lia: quick check — ELB target group shows 60% healthy, connection errors on targets. Dump from ELB: 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-northeast-3:123456:targetgroup/tg-abc/abcd
TargetHealthDescriptions: 3 unhealthy, 5 healthy, UnhealthyReason: 'connection-reset'
```

oncall-sre: running tcpdump on one proxy host, seeing RSTs to/from ENI. Suspect VPC egress path. Asking eng-runtime to validate kernel conntrack.

eng-runtime-bot: noted. quick-check: kernel conntrack table is at 92% on some hosts. We can bump conntrack or cycle NAT gateway.

mike: trying conntrack -S before action: shows high usage and many ESTABLISHED->TIME_WAIT churn for ephemeral ports.

oncall-sre: plan: 1) shift Route53 weights for inference-api.apn3 -> fallback region ap-northeast-1 by 60% 2) add temporary NAT gateway in other AZ 3) drain suspect targets behind ALB 4) open AWS support ticket.

anjali: I can flip Route53. Doing weighted routing change now. Command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://weight-change.json
```
Response: ChangeInfo Id: /change/ABC123 (propagating)

lia: scaling dedicated pools in ap-northeast-1 to absorb 60% traffic, spinning up reserved nodes.

incident-bot: AWS Support case opened: case-id 20260315-APN3-NAT-EGRESS-001. Initial update: "Investigating potential NAT gateway egress issues in ap-northeast-3 AZC affecting TCP connections".

aws-support: we're seeing internal ENI flap correlated with an upstream fabric controller restart in azc. Asking for ENI IDs and instance IDs to correlate.

oncall-sre: posting ENI/instance list in the channel. Starting draining targets on affected AZ.

mike: drain started: 
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:ap-northeast-3:123456:targetgroup/tg-abc/abcd --targets Id=i-0abc1234
```
Target state: draining

lia: after weight change we see overall 5xx drop from 34% -> 8% in 3m. Customer errors reduced but some clients still hit old cache TTLs.

anjali: customer impact: affected customers with dedicated apn3 pools: 4 enterprise tenants saw > 20% errors; we've sent initial incident-notice to CSMs.

oncall-sre: next step reduce conntrack pressure: cycled NAT gateway in azc. Command and output:
```
aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc
aws ec2 create-nat-gateway --subnet-id subnet-xxx --allocation-id eipalloc-yyy
```
New NAT created, route tables updated.

eng-runtime-bot: confirm conntrack counts dropping. ESTABLISHED churn reduced.

incident-bot: Monitoring: error-rate trending down to 2% over 5m. Keeping incident open for 60m for validation.

director-ops: thanks team. please capture timeline and mitigation notes for postmortem. If perf regresses after weight removal we'll reopen.

oncall-sre: handing off to @lia for monitoring for the next 45m. I need to sleep. :sleeping:  

lia: acked. I'll watch dashboards and coordinate with AWS support until case moves to root cause. Will escalate if >5% errors for 10m.

mike: leaving a quick snippet of checks for followup:
- ELB target health (describe-target-health)
- conntrack (cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack)
- NAT gateway metrics (CloudWatch)
- Route53 change status (aws route53 get-change)

oncall-sre: incident-channel archived to #inc-1712009876 after stabilization. Reminder to add postmortem owners: oncall-sre, eng-runtime-bot, network eng.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-001 resolved (stabilized) — duration 72m. Final notes: root cause suspected ENI egress path flapping in azc; mitigation: routed traffic away, cycled NAT, drained targets. Postmortem assigned.
